thread:
Emma: quick heads-up — while bringing up magnet-lite-16k int4 on longloop bench I see small token alignment slips after ~18k tokens. looks like a KV flush/realignment during a shard handoff
Raj: ugh. slip as in repeated token or missing token?
Emma: missing/shifted; e.g. ground-truth 'the quick brown fox' becomes 'the quick brown' then next tokens start one position earlier. not catastrophic but causes downstream eval diffs
Sylvie: any pattern? specific prompt prefixes, or after a certain size?
Emma: seems deterministic for this model/quant profile when rotary index > 16384 and when prefill uses interleaved shard swap. only on int4 config; float32/8bit fine. runs on dedicated-staging-gpu
Mike: can you paste a tiny repro (command + snippet)?
Emma: sure. here's the reproduce command we use in longloop harness:
```bash
./run_longloop --model magnet-lite-16k --quant int4 --prefill-mode interleaved --max-tokens 20000 --seed 42
```
and a minimal prompt we used:
```text
A. <system long primer 16k tokens>\nOnce upon a time, the quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog...
```
Raj: logs? any KV write/read offsets showing mismatch?
Emma: yes, grabbed a tail of the runtime log around the handoff:
```
[2026-04-12T10:15:34Z] KV_WRITE shard=2 offset=16380 len=48
[2026-04-12T10:15:34Z] KV_FLUSH shard=2 next_base=0x7f8a3c len=1024
[2026-04-12T10:15:34Z] ROPE_IDX remap from 16380 -> 0 (wrap)
[2026-04-12T10:15:34Z] TOKEN_EMIT idx=16381 tok=4523
[2026-04-12T10:15:34Z] TOKEN_EMIT idx=0 tok=4499  <- unexpected
```
Sylvie: that remap looks suspicious — ROPE index remapping during flush shouldn't flip the exposed token indices. could be a wrap vs absolute index bug in the int4 kernel that calculates the remap base
Mike: does the runtime do any 'compact' step when quant profile is int4? like shrinking KV index space to compress memory?
Emma: yes, int4 profile triggers compacting/stride packing on warmstart to reduce memory. compact uses a modulo remap for shard offsets. suspect off-by-one in that path
Sylvie: two quick checks: 1) run with --no-compact (if available) to see if it goes away. 2) a diff run with same seed but quant=int8 or float to confirm quant-specific
Emma: did both — int8/float clean. --no-compact reduces frequency but doesn't eliminate slip (so compact+stride seems to exacerbate).
Raj: can we add assert/guard that verifies the expected token index monotonicity across the remap? even if expensive for debug builds
Emma: already added a temp assert in my local build, it tripped showing remap_base computed as 0 for a non-zero expected region
Mike: paste the assert snippet you used
Emma:
```c
// debug guard
if (remap_base == 0 && expected_base != 0) {
  log_warn("remap_base_zero_mismatch expected=%lld computed=%lld", expected_base, remap_base);
  abort();
}
```
Raj: nice. please push as a debug-only patch to the canary branch so CI can run quick per-commit smoke
Sylvie: also check rotatory-scaling multiplication in quant kernel. int4 packing sometimes changes alignment and an int-promote step could overflow the accumulator, leading to wrap-around when computing scaled positions
Emma: good call. I will instrument the int4 position multiply and dump values around the wrap point.

Mike: while you gather instrumented logs, run a lightweight eval comparing token-by-token hash of outputs for the first 20k tokens across profiles. that'll give us a metric (slip_count)
Emma: done locally, slip_count: int4=27, int8=0, float=0 for that same seed/prompt. attaching small table in thread
Sylvie: open a bug (label: kvcache, quant, long-context) and assign to me + Emma. include minimal repro and logs. we should escalate if it's a correctness regression vs expected behavior
Emma: filed BUG-1246 with logs + command + my debug assert output. assigning to Sylvie. link: https://redwood/bugs/1246
Raj: next steps: sylvie to triage root cause, emma to run further instrumented runs for boundary cases, mike to prepare rollback/fallback policy if we need to disable compacting on canary
Sylvie: will triage today. first hypothesis: remap math in compact path + int4 alignment bug -> plan a small unit test for remap arithmetic and a kernel-level replicate
Emma: FYI I also saw a different symptom on a separate run where tokens duplicated (repeat) rather than shifted — seems like two manifestations of the same remap/misalignment
Mike: ok. let's keep the canary off for public traffic until we confirm. set dedicated-staging as quarantine. :warning:
Raj: thanks Emma — great repro. ping me when you have instrument dumps so I can help analyze accumulator math
Emma: will do, posting the instrumented dump when ready (couple mins)
Mike: :thumbsup:
Emma: posted dump gist: https://gist.redwood/abcd1234 — includes int4 pos vals, remap_base traces, and the exact emitted token sequence diffs
Sylvie: got it. preliminary glance matches an off-by-modulus in remap. I'll start a unit test and a small patch for the compact routine; we'll run canary with assert to confirm fix
Raj: nice. keep this thread for updates and link the eventual PR/patch here
Emma: will update. thanks all
Mike: short note for the changelog: "fix: correct KV remap during int4 compacting to preserve RoPE index continuity" if validated
Sylvie: adding to triage board now
